back: When a std::string is passed to a function by value, the std::string function parameter must be instantiated and initialized with the argument. This results in an expensive copy.
front: Why don't you pass std::string by value?

Initializing a std::string is expensiveWhenever a std::string is initialized, a copy of the string used to initialize it is made. Making copies of strings is expensive, so care should be taken to minimize the number of copies made.Do not pass std::string by value
